title: DROPS headline counters SHRANK 22px -> 18px in a 'bigger fonts' PR; the PR table claims counters grew +29%
evidence:
-		noc_col(v, fmt.tprintf("%d", feed.drop_e9), 22, NOC_RED, head_lbl_r + 8, y)
-		noc_col(v, fmt.tprintf("%d", feed.drop_pool), 22, NOC_AMBER, NOC_PANEL_X + NOC_PANEL_W - 6, y)
+		noc_col(v, fmt.tprintf("%d", feed.drop_e9), NOC_SIZE_BODY, NOC_RED, head_lbl_r + 8, y)
+		noc_col(v, fmt.tprintf("%d", feed.drop_pool), NOC_SIZE_BODY, NOC_AMBER, px + NOC_PANEL_W - 6, y)
+NOC_SIZE_BODY  :: 18 // body/counters
detail: The headline numerals were 22px and are now NOC_SIZE_BODY (18px) — an 18% reduction. The committed PR body's ladder table lists 'Body / counters | 18px | 14–15px | +29%', omitting that the largest, most important counters on the panel got smaller.
recommended_fix: Add a headline rung above the title (e.g. NOC_SIZE_HEADLINE 22-24) for the DROPS counters, or correct the PR table to disclose the 22->18 reduction.

title: Cited KYLE requirement '1.5–2× needed' is unmet for labels (12px -> 15px = 1.25×); PR body admits it, then claims KYLE PASS
evidence:
+The 2026-08-23 user verdict (THIRD STRIKE): "still so hard to read — bigger fonts please" + the DOCK-RIGHT ruling. KYLE's live-screen assessment: **1.5–2× needed**
+- **The 15px label rung** — KYLE's 1.5× band on labels is 18px; the ladder's label rung is the ruling's exact 15px, at-or-above the 14px floor (the user's stated minimum).
detail: The diff's own PR body states the 1.5–2× remediation band, then ships labels at 1.25×, rationalizing via 'the ruling's exact 15px'. Verification section then asserts a KYLE legibility PASS. The stated requirement and the shipped rung contradict.
recommended_fix: Either raise the label rung into the cited band or restate the acceptance criterion so the 15px rung is honestly justified against the 1.5–2× assessment.

title: view_set_rail has no floor: win_w < NOC_RAIL_W yields play_w <= 0, and camera_fit then returns a zero/negative scale
detail: Resizing the window below 524px wide with D on makes play_w negative; camera_fit/play_w propagates a negative scale into scale/off_x (degenerate or inverted frame). No clamp or narrow-window fallback exists anywhere in the diff.
recommended_fix: Clamp play_w (e.g. max(1, win_w - NOC_RAIL_W)) or auto-disable the rail below a minimum window width; add a narrow-window test.

title: Press swallow covers the full-height plate including the over-plate top band; only tray chips yield — no yield shown for the pause chip / top-band clickables
detail: The rail rect spans y 0..win_h, and the top band (health card, forecast, pause chip) paints OVER the plate. The swallow yields only for tray_chip_hit. If any top-band element over the plate accepts clicks, it is dead — the same B1'' bug class the tray yield fixed.
recommended_fix: Hit-test and yield for every clickable element that paints over the plate (pause chip, health/forecast cards), or restrict the swallow to the content region below NOC_CONTENT_Y.

title: Rail shrink follows overlay_on, but the draw and the swallow follow overlay_on && stats_valid — D with invalid stats shrinks the playfield with no plate drawn
detail: effect_overlay flips play_w unconditionally; the plate draw requires stats_valid. While stats are invalid (e.g. first frames), the world fits left of an invisible 524px rail — dead screen space with no visual cause and no press ownership.
recommended_fix: Gate view_set_rail on the same condition as the draw (overlay_on && stats_valid), or draw an empty plate whenever the playfield is shrunk.

title: crisis_card_width's 240px floor overrides the new playfield clamp — with the rail on, a narrow window puts the banner outside the playfield
detail: When min(by_forecast, by_playfield) < hud(240), the floor wins and the banner exceeds by_playfield, violating the new 'stays inside the playfield' invariant. The rail (play_w = win_w - 524) raises the breakdown width by ~524px versus the old win_w clamp.
recommended_fix: Cap the floor at the available playfield (max(min(hud(v,240), by_playfield), ...)) or accept and document a minimum supported width with the rail on.
